caption: Past the walls, the road went on being a road.
The debt was settled. He had not planned for the morning after it.
He knew, now, why his father had kept saying yes. It had not made the debt any smaller.
He would never know why his father had kept saying yes. The debt had not required him to.
He kept the ledger. Not for the sums, which were closed. For the hand that wrote them.
A city that never asked his name held it anyway, in a column, in a figure that balanced. He wanted it kept there.
Stripped of every borrowed thing, the floating man still says: I am. He had tested it the long way, and it held.
He kept the ledger and stopped looking for himself in it. The sums were closed either way.
A city that never asked his name held it anyway. He found that he did not need it back.
The self is the last debt, and the only one no creditor comes to collect. He had settled it without being asked.
